title: Errands
eyebrow: requests that cannot be made from a screen
dek: Everything this archive now needs is in a building. Each of these is written up so it can be sent as it stands.
lead:
This archive has read what can be read online. What is left is held in reading rooms, registry offices and one Australian state registry, and it needs a person to ask. **Each errand below gives the exact reference, what to ask for, what it would settle, and a draft in the language the office works in.** Nothing here is speculative: every reference has been checked to exist.

**Verify each institution's current address and request form on its own website before sending.** This page carries references, not addresses — an address copied from memory is exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong.

rows.who: Hrvatski državni arhiv, Zagreb — HR-HDA-1448
rows.what: Crikvenica births 1909–1926 — roll ZM-34J/362, topographic mark M-6957
rows.ref: HR-HDA-1448, Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji; R 1909–1926, Matični ured Crikvenica; digitised
rows.why:
**One roll holds the baptisms of all five of Anton Rudolf and Ursula's children** — Josip Petar 1911, Petar Vid 1913, Anka Nera 1915, Zdravko 1921 and Ivan Anton 1925 — and this archive has not one of them.

FamilySearch's Crikvenica films stop at **Rođeni 1896**, cut at the hundred-year line as it stood when they were made, so every one of those five births falls after the end of the only collection the archive can reach for free. The supplementary collection does not stop there. **This is the single most overdue book in the archive**: five baptisms, one reel, and the parents named on every one of them.

The archive already wanted two other books from the same collection — the twentieth-century **Status animarum** (ZM-34J/251, M-5976), which is a household census that would give the whole family on one page, and **marriages 1909–1947** (the same ZM-34J/362). All three should go in one request.

**Update 27 October 2026.** The finding aid was searched again (Crikvenica, RIMOKATOLICI, kind V) and returns **marriages 1909–1947, Matični ured Crikvenica, roll ZM-34J/362, mark M-6957, digital «Da»** — the same book named above, now with a specific entry to ask for: **Anton Rudolf Defranceschi and Uršula Kovačina, 21 June 1912** (the date is the Geni tree's, `lore`). FamilySearch's marriages for Crikvenica (9R28-3Y9) end in 1908, so this is the only reachable copy. The entry would also test the tree's first son, Josip Petar, born 3 December 1911 — six and a half months earlier.

**Update 3 November 2026 — four more entries that only this roll can give.** (1) **Zorica Defranceski's marriage to Dragutin Jugović, 6 August 1924** (told in the remarks cell of her 1896 baptism entry, Crikvenica births 1895–96 entry 143): the marriage entry would give his age, his parents and hers, and her residence. (2) **Slava Kovačina's marriage to Anton Ivan Stipanić, 14 January 1920** (the remarks cell of 1895 entry 42): it would name her parents, and so settle whether she is Ursula's sister. (3) **Josip Defranceschi's marriage to Ursula Car, 25 January 1913**, marriage book IV page 33 number 4: it would give his birth date and place, which no register read so far gives (the Ledenice births of 1888 were read on 3 November 2026 as far as images 440 to 451 and hold no entry born 26 July). (4) The births of **1897 to 1902 are in no collection at all**: not in FamilySearch (the Crikvenica births end in 1896), and the HDA finding aid lists births 1881 to 1896 and then 1909 to 1926, nothing between; so Slava's own baptism of about 1900, and the births of Ursula's other sisters, cannot be read anywhere online; the marriages above are the way round. The 1965 court file that dissolved Zorica's marriage (Općinski sud u Rijeci, P-725/65-8, decision of 9 December 1965) is not an archive book and is not online; it would have to be asked of the Državni arhiv u Rijeci, if the court's files of that year have been given to it.
rows.ask: A scan or reading copy of the entries for the surname Defranceschi / Defranceski / De Franceschi in Crikvenica births 1909–1926 (ZM-34J/362, M-6957), together with the Crikvenica Status animarum of the twentieth century (ZM-34J/251, M-5976) and Crikvenica marriages 1909–1947 (ZM-34J/362, M-6957); with the folio or image reference for each entry. In the marriages, please look first for the entry of Anton Rudolf Defranceschi (born Klenovica, 1890) and Uršula Kovačina (born Crikvenica, 28 February 1895), thought to be 21 June 1912. Please also look, in the marriages 1909–1947, for: Zorica Defranceski (born Crikvenica 14 December 1896) and Dragutin Jugović, 6 August 1924; Slava Kovačina (born Crikvenica about 1900) and Anton Ivan Stipanić, 14 January 1920; and Josip Defranceschi (born about 1888) and Ursula Car, 25 January 1913, book IV page 33 number 4; and say whether any register of births for Crikvenica for 1897–1908 survives anywhere in the State Archives.
rows.draft:
**To: info@arhiv.hr** (the address on the HDA's own homepage, checked 3 November 2026; written, not sent). Subject: *Zahtjev za preslike upisa: matične knjige Crikvenica 1909.–1947., rola ZM-34J/362 i ZM-34J/251 (HR-HDA-1448)*

Poštovani,

istražujem obitelj Defranceschi / Defranceski / De Franceschi iz Crikvenice i molim Vašu pomoć oko građe iz Zbirke dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji (HR-HDA-1448). U pretrazi matičnih knjiga na Vašim stranicama pronašao sam sljedeće svitke za Crikvenicu: rođeni 1909.–1926. (ZM-34J/362, M-6957), vjenčani 1909.–1947. (ZM-34J/362, M-6957) i Status animarum 20. stoljeća (ZM-34J/251, M-5976), svi digitalizirani.

Molim Vas za preslike (skenove) ili čitljive kopije upisa za prezime Defranceschi / Defranceski / De Franceschi u rođenima 1909.–1926. i u vjenčanima 1909.–1947., kao i stranica Status animarum na kojima se ta obitelj nalazi, sa stranicom ili brojem snimke za svaki upis.

U vjenčanima molim da se prvo potraži upis Antona Rudolfa Defranceschija (rođen u Klenovici 1890.) i Uršule Kovačina (rođena u Crikvenici 28. veljače 1895.), vjerojatno 21. lipnja 1912. Molim i upise: Zorica Defranceski (rođena u Crikvenici 14. prosinca 1896.) i Dragutin Jugović, 6. kolovoza 1924.; Slava Kovačina (rođena u Crikvenici oko 1900.) i Anton Ivan Stipanić, 14. siječnja 1920.; Josip Defranceschi (rođen oko 1888.) i Ursula Car, 25. siječnja 1913., knjiga IV, str. 33, br. 4. Datumi potječu iz obiteljskih i drugih sekundarnih izvora, pa Vas molim da potražite i u okolnim datumima.

Molim Vas i da mi javite postoji li u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu ili drugim državnim arhivima sačuvana matična knjiga rođenih za Crikvenicu za 1897.–1908. Na FamilySearchu rođeni završavaju 1896., a u Vašem pregledu našao sam rođene 1881.–1896. i zatim tek od 1909.

Ako je za naručivanje preslika potreban obrazac ili pristojba, molim Vas da mi javite postupak i iznos.

Unaprijed zahvaljujem na trudu.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski, david.defranceski@gmail.com

rows.who: Biskupijski arhiv Poreč-Pula / Ordinariate of Pola
rows.what: Marriage dispensations for Vodnjan, 1815–1884
rows.ref: Cited in the register itself: «Dispensa … dell'Ordinariato di **Pola**», with numbers — e.g. 18 Feb 1830 № 97
rows.why: The Vodnjan marriage register **cites its own paperwork by number**. Each dispensation file names the degree of kinship and the couple's common ancestor — which is the single fastest way to join the two Vodnjan lines to each other, if they join at all.
rows.ask:
Whether the dispensation files of the Ordinariate of Pola for 1815–1884 survive, and if so how they are arranged and whether they can be consulted or copied by number.

**Sent 14 September 2026** from David's own account (thread 1a09e086d2d5d827). Awaiting a reply.

Vi sarei grato di sapere se questi fascicoli si conservano e come si possono consultare.

rows.who: Matični ured Senj (registry office) / Državni arhiv u Rijeci
rows.what: Senj birth register 1926 — Hedviga Blažević, and the Senj marriage register for 1948
rows.ref: Matična knjiga rođenih Senj 1926; matična knjiga vjenčanih Senj 1948
rows.why: Two things at once. **Hedviga's date of birth stood in this archive as both 8 March 1926 and 3 August 1926** — the same digits in the wrong order. **Settled on 17 September 2026 in favour of 3 August**, on the certified extract of the Senj birth register translated for the Supreme Court of South Africa, with David's tree agreeing; see [correction 108](/corrections/). **The register line is still wanted** — not to fix the date now, but for what an extract never carries: the house number, the parents as the priest wrote them, and the godparents. And **the family remembers 1948** as the year she and Ivan Defranceski «went»; a marriage entry that year would explain the memory without contradicting their son's 1951 birth at Senj.
rows.ask: A certified copy of the birth entry for **Blažević Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj, daughter of Ljubomir Blažević and Milka née Papić; and a search of the 1948 marriage register for **Defranceski Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, with **Blažević Hedviga**.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim Vas ovjereni izvadak iz **matične knjige rođenih za Senj, godina 1926**, za **Hedvigu Blažević**, kćer Ljubomira Blaževića i Milke rođene Papić. Molim i pretragu **matične knjige vjenčanih za Senj, godina 1948**, za **Ivana Defranceskog**, rođenog 25. lipnja 1925. u Crikvenici, i **Hedvigu Blažević**. Istraživanje je obiteljsko i nekomercijalno. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

rows.who: Arolsen Archives (International Tracing Service), Bad Arolsen
rows.what: Any trace of Ivan Defranceski and Hedviga Blažević leaving Yugoslavia, 1948–1951
rows.ref: ITS Digital Collections; the family is already in the Pfullingen list of foreigners and the AOK sickness-fund cards · **Use the inquiry form, not the contact form** — `arolsen-archives.org/en/search-explore/inquiries/submit-inquiry/`. The general *Kontaktanfrage* box on the main site arrives at `documentation@` and gets sent back; the inquiry form opens a numbered case. Required: first name, last name, e-mail, subject, salutation, consent tick, reCAPTCHA · References to quote: CM/1 **3.2.1.1, 32110000 058.158** and T/D case **06030302.0.349.822**.
rows.why:
**Lodged, and it now has a number: tracing inquiry 2026-09-17-60142**, receipt confirmed by Bad Arolsen at 10:11 UTC on 17 September 2026.

**How it got there.** The text sent on 13 September went into the site's general **contact** box — it arrived at `documentation@` as a *Kontaktanfrage*, and on the morning of the 17th they sent it back: *«We would like to ask you to submit your request via the online form.»* Nothing had been searched and nothing refused; it was simply the wrong door. The **inquiry form** at `arolsen-archives.org/en/search-explore/inquiries/submit-inquiry/` is the one that opens a case, and that is where it went in the same day.

**What the case actually contains is one person, not five.** The form takes up to five named people; the submission carries **Ivan Defranceski** alone, fully documented — born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, Brunnenstraße 7 in Pfullingen, parents and wife named, and the four Online Archive records already found for him given by link:

· 2.1.3.1 — *Iwan*, 24.06.1925, birthplace written «Gricivenica» — person/70823303
· 2.2.2.1 War Time Card File — *JVAN*, 25.06.1925 — person/71930658
· 2.3.3.1 — *IWAN*, 25.06.1925 — person/77422349
· 2.3.3.1 — *JWAN*, 24.06.1925 — person/77422350

**Hedviga Blažević is in it by name but not as a listed person** — she is named as his wife and the request for 1948–1951 asks for her IRO file in the same breath. **Uršula Kovačina, Anton Rudolf, and Petar's CM/1 file are not in this case at all.** They are the next inquiry, and the two references to quote are already written down: **CM/1 3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158** and **T/D 349.822, ref 06030302.0.349.822**.

**What was asked.** The wartime card itself, and any IRO registration, screening, counselling or rejection file for Ivan or Hedviga in the French occupation zone — Württemberg-Hohenzollern, Kreis Reutlingen, Pfullingen — for **1948–1951**.

**Why that window and not another.** The family's testimony is that Ivan and Hedviga **left in 1948 meaning not to come back**; their son was born at Senj on 17 December 1951, which puts them home by about March 1951. **A failed exit leaves nothing in a Croatian register.** If it survives anywhere, it survives at Bad Arolsen.

**Expect months, not weeks.** Their own acknowledgement says processing may take several months, and the form's banner warns of up to thirteen.
rows.ask: A search of the ITS holdings for **1948–1951** for **DEFRANCESKI / DEFRANCESCHI, Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, and **BLAŽEVIĆ, Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj — in the **French zone (Württemberg-Hohenzollern, Reutlingen and Pfullingen)** and in any IRO registration, screening or rejection file. Separately: **KOVAČINA, Uršula**, born about 1890; and confirmation of which **Anton Rudolf Defranceski** appears on the 1947 Pfullingen list and the 1950 mayoral certificate, since the family records him as dying in **1943**. Also, by reference rather than by name: copies from the **CM/1 personal file 3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158** (*DEFRANCESKI, Petar, b. 15 June 1913, and of further persons*), and from **T/D case 349.822**, ref 06030302.0.349.822, together with a note of what is withheld there and why. **Still to be lodged as a second inquiry:** Uršula Kovačina (b. about 1895, Crikvenica, died Belgrade 1975); Anton Rudolf Defranceski (b. 20 January 1890, Klenovica house 22 — on the 1947 Pfullingen list and the 1950 mayoral certificate, although the family records him dead in 1943); and Petar Vid Defranceski by reference — **CM/1 3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158** and **T/D 349.822, ref 06030302.0.349.822**.
rows.draft: Dear Arolsen Archives, I am researching my own family and have already used your Pfullingen list of foreigners and the Allgemeine Ortskrankenkasse card for Ivan Defranceski (Brunnenstraße 7, Pfullingen, from 21 October 1941). I should be grateful for a search of the ITS holdings for the years **1948–1951** for **DEFRANCESKI / DEFRANCESCHI, Ivan**, born 25 June 1925 at Crikvenica, Croatia, and for **BLAŽEVIĆ, Hedviga**, born 1926 at Senj — including any **IRO registration, screening or rejection** file in the French zone (Reutlingen / Pfullingen). His brothers **Zdravko** and **Anton** resettled to Australia from there in 1949 (Anton's card is stamped «Emigré Australie le 8.3.49»). I am also looking for **KOVAČINA, Uršula**, born about 1890, and for clarification of the **Anton Rudolf Defranceski** named on the 1947 Pfullingen list and certified by the mayor in 1950. Non-commercial family research. Two references from your own collections, in case they save you a search: the CM/1 personal file **3.2.1.1, ref 32110000 058.158**, «Personal file of DEFRANCESKI, PETAR, born 15 June 1913 … and of further persons», and the tracing and documentation case **T/D 349.822**, ref **06030302.0.349.822** (collection 6.3.3.2, 8 documents, 1954–1984), of which parts are not displayed online. I should be grateful for copies of whatever may be released from either, and for a note of what is withheld and why.

rows.who: Matični ured Crikvenica / Župni ured Crikvenica
rows.what: The death of Anton Rudolf Defranceski, said by the family to be 1943 — and the surname Car
rows.ref: Matična knjiga umrlih Crikvenica 1943; and register entries for the surname **Car**, 1930s–1950s
rows.why:
This archive holds **two facts that cannot both be true**: Anton Rudolf Defranceski, born 20 January 1890 at Klenovica house 22, is recorded as having **died in 1943** «per the family», and is also on the **Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947** and **certified by that town's mayor in 1950**. Everything the family remembers about his widow depends on which is right.

The same request covers **Car** — the surname the family remembers as «Carr», which on this coast is far more likely to be the Croatian **Car**.
rows.ask: A search of the Crikvenica death register for **1943** for **Defranceski / Defranceschi, Anton Rudolf**, born 20 January 1890; and any entry linking the surname **Car** with **Kovačina, Uršula**, born 28 February 1895, in the 1940s.
rows.draft: Poštovani, molim Vas pretragu **matične knjige umrlih za Crikvenicu, godina 1943.**, za **Antona Rudolfa Defranceskog**, rođenog 20. siječnja 1890. u Klenovici, kućni broj 22. Molim i svaki upis koji povezuje prezime **Car** s **Uršulom Kovačina**, rođenom oko 1890., tijekom 1940-ih. Riječ je o obiteljskom istraživanju.

rows.who: Muzej Grada Crikvenice / Novi list archive, Rijeka
rows.what: Hedviga Blažević, a singer at the Hotel Therapia, Crikvenica, 1940s
rows.ref: Hotel Therapia (1895 Nadvojvoda Josip; Therapia from c.1899; latterly Falkensteiner, now Kvarner Palace) — programmes, posters, season photographs
rows.why: The family names the venue: **Hedviga sang at the Hotel Therapia**. That is the building that made Crikvenica a health resort — opened **1895** as the *Nadvojvoda Josip*, renamed **Therapia** when a hydropathic institute was installed. She was a **Senj** woman and Ivan a **Crikvenica** man, and this is the first explanation this archive has ever had for how the two towns met. It would also give a woman recorded here only as a wife, a mother and a date of death **a profession and a workplace**.
rows.ask:
Any programme, poster, photograph or press notice naming a singer **Hedviga Blažević** at the **Hotel Therapia**, Crikvenica, between about 1944 and 1952 — including the hotel's own season programmes for those years.

**Answered 12 September 2026 by the hotel itself.** Almost nothing survives from the Therapia years — no guest books, no personnel records, no programmes — and the present owners had already searched for the same material when they took the hotel over. They do not know where it went. **The hotel is eliminated; the museum and the Novi list archive are not.**
rows.draft: Poštovani, tražim bilo kakav program, plakat, fotografiju ili novinsku vijest u kojoj se spominje pjevačica **Hedviga Blažević** u **hotelu Therapia** u Crikvenici, otprilike između 1944. i 1952. godine — uključujući i sezonske programe samoga hotela za te godine. Riječ je o obiteljskom istraživanju, nekomercijalnom. Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Zadru (State Archive in Zadar)
rows.what: The Governor's Office surveillance file on Valente Defranceschi, editor of «La Trappola», 1867
rows.ref: Namjesništvo / I. R. Luogotenenza della Dalmazia — **501 IX 2/2 1097**, report of 19 September 1867; related item **493 IX 2/3 63**, 1866
rows.why:
**The first police record of this surname anywhere in the archive, and the likeliest document to give a nineteenth-century Zadar De Franceschi a father.** A political surveillance report of the 1860s normally records the subject's age, birthplace, family and employment, because that is what the officer was required to write down. rows.who: Österreichisches Staatsarchiv — Kriegsarchiv, Vienna
rows.what: Officer personnel sheets for six men of the name, 1859–1918 — and a €45 quote the catalogue has half-answered
rows.ref: Kriegsarchiv, Personalunterlagen — **Grundbuchblätter**, arranged by regiment and year of birth
rows.why:
**This is the document that would turn nine service entries into genealogy.** The Austrian and Hungarian printed service lists give a man's year of birth, his unit and his seniority — and never his birthplace. The *Grundbuchblatt* gives **birthplace, parents, religion, marriage and next of kin**. Six men of this name served in units this archive can now name, and not one of them can currently be attached to a household.

The prize is **Julius**: born 1879, in service from 1 July 1898, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine, still on the active list in July 1918. If he is a Fiume or Bakar man, his sheet says so, and the Kvarner households acquire their first documented officer.

---

**Answered on 17 September 2026, and the answer splits the six men in two.** The Direktion des Kriegsarchivs replies under **Geschäftszahl 2026-0.769.907**, signed by the Archivdirektor at Vienna on 16 September, and heads the letter *«Marinepersonensuche Julis Defranceschi (\*1879) und Valentin Defranceschi (im Dienst 1854–1856)»* — **the two sailors, and only the two sailors.**

**For the navy men they offer a paid search.** €45 per started half-hour, *the first half-hour free*; they estimate an hour, so **€45**. The fee is payable **whether or not anything is found** — they say so in their own sentence, and it is the sentence that matters. Results are consulted in person in the Forschersaal at Nottendorfer Gasse 2–4, or sent as scans; only digital reproductions are made, for conservation, and up to **€40** of reproduction costs are taken as agreed unless refused in advance. Acceptance is by e-mail to `ka@oesta.gv.at`, after which they send a costing with bank details. **This is David's to accept or decline; nothing here commits him.**

**For the four land-forces men they offer nothing — and that is the useful half.** Theodor, Alois, Eduard and Dr Cäsar Peschle are waved at the Kriegsarchiv's own *«Forschungstipps (FAQ)»*, which they say lists **all already-digitised holdings** for self-study. Read plainly: **the army material this archive wants may already be online and free**, and nobody here has looked. That is now [a work-list item](/worklist/) rather than an errand.

**One question the letter does not answer** is the one the enquiry led with — whether **Eduard**, cadet 1859 and Unterleutnant 1863, is one man or two. It asks for a fee before saying.

---

**20 September: the catalogue answers the bill.** The ÖStA's own free field search — `archivinformationssystem.at/feldsuche.aspx`, no account, no fee — was run for the first time and returns **99 records on the stem, 53 of them this name**. Two of them decide this errand.

**Do not buy a search for Valentin.** He is catalogued to the item: **AT-OeStA/KA Marine NMA PA Offiziere und Beamte Akten QL 944 — DEFRANCESCHI, Valentin, Administrations-Assistent**, a naval *Qualifikationsliste*, marked *«Permission required: Keine · Accessibility: Öffentlich»*. The right request is the one in their own FAQ — *«Ich möchte digitale Reproduktionen von Archivalien bestellen»* — quoting the signature. **A file you can cite is a retrieval, not a research fee.**

**And Julius is very probably not there to find.** He is absent from the catalogue, and the Kriegsarchiv's own navy page explains it: personnel records of men **born after 1865** whose *Heimatzuständigkeit* lay outside today's Austria *«verblieben in den jeweiligen Nachfolgestaaten bzw. wurden dorthin abgetreten»*. **Julius was born in 1879 on the Kvarner.** His Qualifikationsliste went to Yugoslavia at the dissolution — which means Zagreb or Belgrade, not Vienna. The €45 is payable whether or not anything is found.

**So the reply to `ka@oesta.gv.at` writes itself, and it is cheaper than the quote**: decline the *Marinepersonensuche*, order a reproduction of **QL 944**, and ask them to confirm in one line whether anything for a man born 1879 with Fiume/Bakar *Heimatzuständigkeit* could still be in Vienna before any fee is incurred. Quote **GZ 2026-0.769.907**.
rows.ask:
Grundbuchblätter, or any surviving personnel file, for:
· **Defranceschi, Julius**, b. 1879, k. u. k. Kriegsmarine, service from 1/7/1898, Linienschiffsleutnant with seniority 1/1/1909.
· **Defranceschi, Theodor**, K. K. Landwehr, Fähnrich (nichtaktiv), 27th Regiment, seniority 1 January 1907.
· **Defranceschi, Alois**, k. u. k. Heer, infantry cadet/Fähnrich, listed 1916–1918.
· **Defranceschi, Eduard**, K. K. line infantry, cadet 1859, Unterleutnant 2. Classe 1863 — **and whether this is one man or two**.
· **Defranceschi, Valentin**, K. K. Kriegs-Marine, Marine-Direktion Pola, 1854–1856.
· **Peschle, Cäsar, Dr**, K. K. Landwehr medical officer, commissioned 1 August 1895, 5th and 23rd Regiments, Landsturm district Görz.

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku
rows.what: Who Pietro Defranceschi of Ragusa was, and the Persich–Defranceschi marriage of about 1850
rows.ref: Matične knjige grada Dubrovnika; and the records of the Republic to 1808
rows.why:
**Ragusa was its own republic until 1808, with its own archive, and this project has never asked it a single question.** It now has a reason to.

Four indexed records resolve into one household: **Matteo Persich**, born 1829, son of Antonio Persich and Teresa Martecchini, married **Marietta (Maria) Defranceschi**, daughter of **Pietro Defranceschi**, and their children were baptised at Dubrovnik in 1853, 1863 and 1871.

Marietta is the only Defranceschi here whose existence is certain, and she is documented entirely through her husband and her children. **Her father is a name on one flattened index row and nothing else.** Who he was, when he came, and whether he was one of a family or alone in the city, is completely unknown.
rows.ask:
Three things, in order of usefulness:
· The **marriage entry** of Matteo Persich and Marietta / Maria Defranceschi, probably between 1848 and 1853. A marriage entry names both sets of parents and usually the bride's age and birthplace.
· Any **baptism or death entry** for a **Pietro Defranceschi** at Dubrovnik in the first half of the nineteenth century.
· Whether the surname **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** appears at all in the city's registers or in the Republic's own records before 1808.
rows.draft:
Poštovani,

istražujem obitelj **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** i u indeksima sam pronašao skupinu upisa iz Dubrovnika koji se čini da pripadaju jednoj obitelji:

· **Matteo Persich**, rođen 1829., sin Antonija Persicha i Terese Martecchini;
· njegova supruga **Marietta (Maria) Defranceschi**, kći **Pietra Defranceschija**;
· djeca krštena u Dubrovniku **1853., 1863. i 1871.** (Antonio; Cattarina Teresa Vittoria Maria, 23. prosinca 1863.; Giustino Antonio Alberto Lucciano, 26. rujna 1871.).

Molim Vas pomoć oko tri pitanja:

1. Postoji li **upis vjenčanja** Mattea Persicha i Mariette / Marije Defranceschi, vjerojatno između 1848. i 1853.? Upis vjenčanja navodi roditelje oboje mladenaca te dob i mjesto rođenja nevjeste, što mi je najvažnije.
2. Nalazi li se u maticama grada **Pietro Defranceschi** — krštenje, vjenčanje ili smrt — u prvoj polovici 19. stoljeća?
3. Pojavljuje li se prezime **Defranceschi / De Franceschi** uopće u dubrovačkim maticama ili u spisima Republike prije 1808.?

Riječ je o privatnom obiteljskom istraživanju bez komercijalne svrhe. Rado ću platiti naknadu za preslike prema Vašem cjeniku.

Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski
rows.reply:
**ANSWERED 28 September 2026 — and the answer is that the archive no longer holds the books.** Kornelija Bašica, *viši arhivist*, replying for the Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku:

> *«Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku predao je sve matične knjige Biskupskom ordinarijatu u Dubrovniku, tako da traženo gradivo nije kod nas.»*

**The State Archive has handed over ALL the parish registers to the Diocesan Ordinariate at Dubrovnik**, and refers the enquiry to **arhiv@db.hr**, telephone 020 324 913.

**None of the three questions is answered.** The marriage of Matteo Persich and Marietta Defranceschi, the identity of her father Pietro, and whether the surname appears in the Republic's own records before 1808 are all exactly where they were — but the door has moved, and this is the kind of fact that costs somebody else a fortnight if it is not written down. *(**doc** — the reply is in Gmail thread 1a09cf406b8c46ff.)*

**Note what the reply does NOT say.** It speaks only of the *matične knjige*. The Republic's own archive to 1808 — the third question, and the one only this institution can answer — is not mentioned, and it is not a parish register. That half of the errand is still theirs and is worth asking again, separately and narrowly.
rows.next: Two letters where there was one, and **neither is sent**: the registers to **arhiv@db.hr** (Biskupski ordinarijat Dubrovnik), and the pre-1808 Republic question back to the state archive, narrowed to the fonds it kept.

**Mione (twelve files, 420 images):** one marriage — Osvaldo × Appolonia, 1808 — plus a new generation (**Matteo**, through the daughter Orsola, 1809), a **priest** of the surname in 1785, and a **godfather** in 1789. Four of the twelve turned out to be covering letters, not allegati.

**The other fourteen files (296 images):** no De Franceschi at all — but **three Istrian documents**: Cittanova and Verteneglio 1806, Capodistria 1807, San Lorenzo near Pirano 1807.

**Since then, the Mione registers themselves.** The whole **death series 1806–1815** has been read, and the **marriage tables for 1813 and 1814**. Finds: Anna de Franceschi dead at forty-four in 1815, her husband **Paolo** alive and signing in 1812, **Osvaldo** signing twice at Muina in 1814, and **«Erman de' Franceschi»** shown to be one name and not two families.

**What remains open:** *Matrimoni* 1812 and 1815 and the six *Nati* volumes — the acts these allegati support, which would date the 1809 Cramaro marriage and might name Orsola's mother Maddalena's family. And the **Pieve di Gorto baptismal books at Luincis**, which every one of these extracts was copied out of.

rows.who: Archivio storico della Curia arcivescovile di Udine · and the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto, Luincis di Ovaro
rows.what: The Gorto parish registers — baptisms 1811–1815, and everything before 1806
rows.ref: Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto (Luincis, Ovaro), the mother church of the Val di Gorto — Mione, Muina, Agrons, Ovasta, Luint, Cella and Liariis all baptised there
rows.why:
**The civil births stop at 1810 and this archive can go no further without the church.**

Mione's Napoleonic registers run 1806 to 1815 for marriages, banns and deaths. **The Nati run four volumes and stop** — 1806, 1808, 1809, 1810. Anyone born to these households between **1811 and 1815** is in the Gorto baptismal register or nowhere.

**And 1807 is missing from every Mione series — though not from Ovaro, whose marriages run 1806 to 1815 unbroken.** It is not missing from the year: the marriage index for 1806–1810 records *«Prencis Valentina con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Mione — 6 Agosto 1807»*. **A wedding whose act is not in the archive.** Gorto would have the church record of the same marriage — and it is worth trying the Ovaro 1807 allegati (an_ua679993) first, which costs nothing.

**Before 1806 there is no civil registration at all.** Paolo the carpenter, Osvaldo *fa legname*, Francesco the tailor, Matteo the shoemaker and Felice Santo the weaver were all born before the French arrived. Their baptisms are at Gorto, and so is the generation above them — which is the generation that would meet the 1679 weavers' list.

*The family has stood in this churchyard and photographed the stones.* What has never been asked for is the register inside.
rows.ask:
Whether the pre-1806 baptismal, marriage and death registers of the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto survive; where they are held — the parish, the diocesan archive at Udine, or the Archivio di Stato; and whether entries for **De Franceschi / Defranceschi / de' Franceschi of Mione, Muina and Agrons** can be copied or consulted. Specifically:

**(a) baptisms 1811–1815**, to close the gap the civil registers leave · **(b) the marriage of Osvaldo Defranceschi and Valentina Prencis, 6 August 1807**, whose Mione civil volume is lost · **(c) baptisms about 1780–1795** for Paolo, Osvaldo, Francesco, Matteo and Felice Santo.

rows.who: David, with a message — any male-line DeFranceschi of the Gračišće reunion families, or of the Crikvenica and Klenovica households
rows.what: One Y-DNA test on a De Franceschi who is not descended from David's father
rows.ref: Y-DNA — FamilyTreeDNA Y-37 or better, or a 23andMe / MyHeritage kit read for its paternal haplogroup
rows.why:
**L-M27 is the single most surprising line in this archive and it currently rests on one father and one son.**

David and Ivan both return **L-M27** — on two different companies' chips — and it is a South Asian lineage that does not appear in the Croatian reference sample at all and shows up **five times in six thousand Italians**. Ivan is 99.9% European autosomally with 0.0% of anything else. **The haplogroup has no autosomal corroboration whatsoever.**

Father and son agreeing proves only that they are father and son. **It cannot distinguish between a De Franceschi male line that has carried L-M27 since before the surname existed, and a non-paternal event anywhere in the last two hundred years** — at Klenovica, at Crikvenica, at Gračišće, at Gologorica, at Mione.

**One test on a second male line settles it, and nothing else will.**
— If another documented male-line De Franceschi is **also L-M27**, the lineage is the surname's and the two lines' common ancestor carried it.
— If he is **not**, the break lies between him and David, and the registers say exactly where the two lines part.

*23andMe's DNA Relatives runs to its 1,500-match cap and contains no living match of the surname.* The father's side clusters instead on Croatian littoral surnames — Miškulin, Vrkljan, Katalinić, Prpić-forms, Serich. **There is no shortcut through the match lists; it has to be asked for.**
rows.ask:
A male De Franceschi / DeFranceschi / Defranceski who descends **father-to-son** from one of:

**(a) Antonio DeFranceschi of Gallignana (1856–1924)** — the Eleven. His sons Antonio, Giuseppe, Gioacchino, Basilio, Rotilio, Pasquale, Nicefaro and Daniele went to New York, Tuscany and Brooklyn, and the 2012 Crystal Springs reunion album names their descendants. **This is the best-documented second line and the one to ask first.**

**(b) the Crikvenica and Klenovica households** — Ivan De Franceschi's line, and the Klenovica house 22 family.

**(c) the Gologorica pedigree** — any surviving male line off the Gologorica book.

What is needed is only the **paternal haplogroup**, not a whole kit. A cousin who has already tested at 23andMe or MyHeritage can read it off his own account in a minute; nobody needs to buy anything.
rows.draft:
Hello — I'm building a documented family history of the De Franceschi line out of Istria and Carnia, and there's one question I can't answer on my own.

My father and I have both had our **paternal (Y-DNA) haplogroup** read, and we come back the same. The Y chromosome passes father to son unchanged, so **every man who descends father-to-son from the same De Franceschi ancestor should carry the same one** — and at the moment I have only my own line to go on.

If you have tested with 23andMe, MyHeritage, Ancestry or FamilyTreeDNA, would you be willing to tell me what your **paternal haplogroup** is? It is one short code — nothing about health, nothing about relatives, and I don't need access to your account.

Whatever it says, I'll tell you what it means for both our lines.

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA) — microfilm ZM34K-216
rows.what: The rest of the Gračišće baptism book — the reel the family's copy stops one frame short of
rows.ref: DAPA microfilm **ZM34K-216**, continuing *Matična knjiga rođenih, Župa Gračišće, 1746–1840*, signatura **3.2**, from **M01070239** to **M01070310**
rows.why:
**The family already holds ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215 and has read them. The book they most need runs off the end of 215.** *Its last written page, M01070226, is headed* **«Annus 1807»**; *the next frame is a printed card reading* **«NASTAVLJA SE»** — *to be continued*. **Everything after 1807 is on ZM34K-216.**

**What is on the missing reel:**

· **Francisca's baptism, 3 February 1819**, of **Gračišće house 5** — the house of **Giovanni Battista Defranceschi**, the farmer of the direct line's second generation. *She married into Gologorica house 6 in 1840 and the census records her born a Defranceschi out of house 5. **If the baptism names her parents, it joins the Gologorica line to the direct line by marriage** — and if it does not, the join is withdrawn.*

· ~~Francisca Salomon's baptism, 17 March 1797~~ — **withdrawn 16 November 2026: it is on the reel the family already holds** (ZM34K-215, M01070211, house 132, Joannes and Maria Salamon; the child's name cell is unsettled). *[The Salomon line](/maternal/salomon/) tells it.* What ZM34K-216 can still give her line is the 1819 baptism of her **daughter** and the later books.

· **The Gračišće births of the direct line's own generations after 1807**, including **Antonio the stonecutter, born 20 September 1825**.

**And the book gives mothers' maiden surnames as a matter of course** — the Matres column is written *«Maria **olim** Zelich»*, *«Maria Milotich **olim** Tirol»* — so this one reel would answer the married-in question for the whole parish, not just for this family.

---

**⭐ 6 October 2026 — AND THERE IS NO ONLINE ROUTE. This was tested twice, three weeks apart, by two different methods.**

*David asked whether Gračišće could be reached on FamilySearch instead of by letter.* **It cannot.**

· **15 September**, *[all 3,488 FamilySearch collections walked](/searched/)* — 44 opened, «Austria, Catholic Church Records» and «Hungary, Civil Registration» tested by name against a control: ***«Gračišće, Gologorica and Pićan are filmed nowhere at all.»***

· **22 September**, *independently, [the Record Atlas's](../Record Atlas) harvest of FamilySearch's open browse endpoint* — **1,733 collections, 4.25 million volumes: 0 hits** *for Gračišće, Gallignana or Gracisce.*

**⭐ And the shape of the gap is the argument for writing.** *«Croatia, Church Books, 1516–1994» holds* **Pazin, Krbune, Tinjan, Svetvinčenat, Barban, Vodnjan, Ližnjan, Poreč, Rovinj, Labin, Buzet** *— Istria is well covered. The parishes it omits are* ***Gračišće, Gologorica, Cerovlje, Pićan and Lindar:*** **precisely the parishes on the DAPA ZM34K reels.** *FamilySearch never filmed this series. DAPA holds it and nobody else published it — which is why a reel this family already buys from one source is the only way to the rest of the book.*

---

**⭐ 7 October 2026 — what a full sweep of the reel's own half adds to this request.** *The* Pater *column of the filmed portion was read across* **thirty-six consecutive frames, M01070190–M01070226 — 1783 to May 1808, roughly nine hundred baptisms — and there is not one Defranceschi father in it.* *⚠* **Corrected 9 October:** *that father-column nil is real, but [the* **Patrini** *column of the same frames was never read, and it holds about twenty Defranceschi, almost all entered* «**Cives**»](/corrections/). ***So the family WAS at Gračišće — as townspeople, continuously from at least 1791 — and simply had no child baptised there before 1808.*** **So the missing reel is not merely where two baptisms sit — it is where the family's ARRIVAL at Gračišće should become visible**, *and that is worth saying to the archive if a reason is ever asked for.*

*(Precision for the letter: the last written page M01070226 is* **headed** «Annus 1807» *but its entries run on to* «**18 Maij**» **1808**.)*

---

**⭐⭐ 11 October 2026 — the 1862 Gologorica census confirms Francisca from the other end, and sharpens what to ask for.** *[Swept end to end](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done), it enters* «**Francisca ux. n. Defranceschi**» *with a birth of* **3 February 1819** *— the date already in this request — and adds a* **death of 8 February 1892**, *a marriage of* **25 February 1840**, *and an* Adnotatio *reading* «***Gallignanensis***». *Her husband is* «**Defranceschi Antonius**» *(1814–1893), whose own* Adnotatio *reads* «***Ex Italia (Carnia)***» *and whose household carries the byname* «**Osvaldo**».

***So the Gračišće bride and the Carnian husband are one household, and both halves are now dated.*** **That is worth saying in the letter**: *the baptism being asked for is of a woman whose marriage, death and parish of origin are all independently attested, which makes her easy for an archivist to find and hard to confuse with a namesake.*

**The book that ends names the book that follows.** *[The Gologorica death register 1784–1880 was walked end to end on 6 October](/searched/) — M01069226 to M01069297, cover to last written page. Its final entry is* **23 January 1880**, *and beneath it, in Italian where the book is Latin:*

> «***Segue libro nuovo · Vol. IV***»

***So Volume IV exists, the parish said so, and it is on neither reel this family owns.***

**⭐ IT CLOSES THE LAST OPEN DEATH-YEAR COLLISION.** *[Worklist 177 carried four](/worklist/); three are now closed — [the burial register took two](/corrections/) and [a census took the third](/gologorica-line/#golo87).* ***The fourth cannot be closed by any book on these reels***: «[Antonius Defranceschi](/who/antonius-defranceschi/)», *born* **3 February 1855**, *is given* **1913** *by a baptism-register margin and* **1918** *by the family tree.* **A death in 1913 or 1918 is in Vol. IV and nowhere else.**

**⭐⭐ AND IT WOULD TURN A DOZEN CENSUS DATES INTO BURIAL ENTRIES.** *[The 1862* status animarum, *swept end to end on 11 October](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done), *carries deaths in its* Obitus *column that this archive has from no register at all:*

| | died |
|---|---|
| «**Clotilda n. Ortis**», *wife of Carlo's brother* | **27 February 1881** |
| «**Francisca ux. n. Defranceschi**», «Gallignanensis» | **8 February 1892** |
| «**Defranceschi Antonius**», *bynamed* «Osvaldo» | **6 January 1893** |
| «**Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi**», *Carlo's brother* | **4 January 1893** |
| «**Ruža n. Salamon**», *[who married three Defranceschi brothers](/gologorica-line/#rosasalamon)* | **17 June 1898** |

***Every one of those is a census clerk's note, not a burial entry.*** *Vol. IV would give the day, the age, the cause and the officiating priest for the whole group — and [this archive's standing rule is that a burial entry is first-hand where a margin and a tree are not](/worklist/).*

⚠ **What is NOT wanted from it:** *an Aloysius Defranceschi dying* **25 November 1870**. *[That date is a marriage, not a death, and the confusion is now filed](/corrections/).*

---

**⭐ 11 October 2026 — a PARTIAL substitute exists, and it narrows the ask rather than cancelling it.** *[The 1894* status animarum *carries an* «**EXTREMA UNCTIO**» *register](/gologorica-line/#sa1894done) (M01069740): last rites by year —* **1907, 1908, 1909** *— each entry with a house, a hamlet and a* ***full date of birth***. *Extreme unction is given at the point of death, so those three years are partly covered without Vol. IV.* ⚠ ***No Defranceschi is among its twenty-three entries***, *and it stops at 1909.* **The request stands:** *the deaths this errand lists run from* **1881 to 1917**, *and all but three of those years are untouched by it.*

**[Errands 35, 36 and 37](/errands/#errand-35) are three separate asks to the same office.** *They were drafted separately because they were found separately; they should not be posted separately.* ***This row is the single letter that carries all three***, *and it is the one to send.*

**⭐ Why now.** *As of 11 October 2026 the family's two reels are* ***read end to end*** — *[the Gologorica baptisms](/gologorica-line/#mkrindex), [its deaths](/gologorica-line/#deathsindexstops), [all four* status animarum*](/gologorica-line/#sa1894done), [Cerovlje](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah) and [both Gračišće baptism books](/searched/). There is nothing substantial left on them.* **Everything the archive now wants is off-reel**, *and it is all held at Pazin.*

**What the letter would settle, in one line each:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **ZM34K-216** | *the baptisms of* **Joanna (1818)** *and* **Francisca (1819)**, *the two Defranceschi brides out of Gračišće houses 4 and 5 — [and whether they were cousins](/worklist/)* |
| **Vol. IV** | *the* ***last open death-year collision*** *(Antonio, 1913 against 1918) and [eight deaths this archive has only from a census clerk's note](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done)* |
| **ZM34K-217** | *house 4 — [the one of the two intermarrying Gračišće houses this archive cannot see](/errands/#errand-37)* |

⚠ **It also says what is NOT wanted**, *which keeps an archivist from hunting a ghost:* [an Aloysius Defranceschi dying 25 November 1870 does not exist — that date is his wedding](/corrections/).

⚠ *A partial substitute for part 2 has since turned up — [the 1894 book carries an* «Extrema unctio» *register for 1907–1909](/gologorica-line/#sa1894done) — but it covers three years of a thirty-seven-year gap and holds no Defranceschi, so the request stands.*

---

**⭐⭐⭐ 11 October 2026 — A FOURTH REQUEST, and it may be the most valuable of them.** *[Looking for one woman's father, this archive checked where the Gologorica marriage register is](/gologorica-line/#mariannaburial).* **The two reels hold exactly one**, *inside the composite at M01068953–M01069007:* «Notatio Personarum Matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ Julij **1770**», *running to* **February 1788**. ***There is no Gologorica marriage register after February 1788 on either reel*** — *a hundred and thirty years of marriages off-film, and this archive had not recorded the gap.*

⚠ **It is not abstract.** *Nearly every marriage date found this week came from a* Matrimonii *column in a census, never from a marriage entry — Aloysius × Joanna 1870, Franciscus × Clotilda 1859, Leonardus 1871 and 1883, Ruža's three, Beatrix 1887, Clotildis Adelaidis 1890, Rosalia × Bubić 1869.* ***A census gives the DATE of a marriage; a marriage entry gives the PARENTS of both parties.*** *That is what this archive keeps running out of.*

⚠ **11 October, later — a partial substitute exists for requests 2 and 4 both, and it argues for the letter rather than against it.** *[The baptism register's margins carry death crosses running to 1954 and* «**Extr. za ženidbu**» *notes dating marriage certificates](/gologorica-line/#baptismmargins).* ***They are annotations, not entries***: *a death cross gives a date and no cause, age, house or officiant; a marriage extract dates the* **certificate**, *not the wedding, and names neither spouse.* **They are enough to show what the missing books would hold, and not enough to replace them.**

rows.ref: Trsat parish death register 1803–1815 (FamilySearch has 9R2F-ZNP to 1803 and 9R2F-ZNG from Nov 1815, nothing between) · Bakar deaths 9R28-DPV, Aug–Dec 1808, already read: nil
rows.why:
**Answered 6 November 2026 by the Rijeka State Archives (*doc* for what they say; letter KLASA 611-03/26-42/2184, URBROJ 126-02-01/1-26-2, signed by the head, Markus Leideck; it reached David's e-mail on 9 November):** the archive «carried out the research» and found that in the death register of the parish of St George, Trsat, **no death of the said Josip Defranceschi, parish priest at Draga, is entered for 1803–1815**. It holds **digital copies** of that book and does not know where the original is kept. The Trsat friary had said on 5 November that the parish holds only post-war books. **What this is and is not:** a statement by the archive, giving no spellings tried, no pages and no entry numbers, so it is *their* nil, not one walked here (the digital copy has not been read by this archive); and a priest of Draga may be entered under another form of the name or under his office alone. His burial is therefore still not found: not Bakar (August–December 1808, read), not Trsat (per the archive), not Draga (no death book before 1815).

**Josephus (Josip) Defranceschi, parish priest of Draga 1798–1808, has no burial.** *Every Draga book on FamilySearch has been read for him (births, marriages, deaths, 4 November 2026) and none holds it.* **What is documented (`doc`):** he writes the Draga baptism book until 13 September 1808; on **29 September 1808** a Trsat Franciscan marries a couple *«de licentia M.R.D. Parochi Dragensis, qui actu infirmitate … Josephi Defranceschi»* with the foot note *«ob impotentiam Dni Parochi»*; and his successor Xanich calls him *«mei Praedecessoris Parochi defuncti»* in 1827. **So he died in the last days of September 1808 (`inf`).** The Draga dead were buried at **Trsat and Bakar** (no cemetery at Draga until 30 September 1855). Bakar, August–December 1808, is nil. **Trsat's death book is on FamilySearch for 1737–1803 and from November 1815, but not for 1803–1815: that gap is the question.**

**This is a follow-up to [errand 4](/errands/#errand-4)**, which asked this office about HR-DARI-254 and HR-DARI-382 and has no reply recorded. If that letter is still waiting, send this one as its second paragraph rather than as a second envelope. **[The Franciscan letter, errand 40,](/errands/#errand-40) asks the same question of the convent**; the book may be at either.
rows.ask:

Fees and postage will be paid.*

⚠ ***Gmail draft saved 4 November 2026, not sent:*** *to **pisarnica@riarhiv.hr**, the e-mail the archive prints on its own homepage (riarhiv.hr); postal address Park Nikole Hosta 2, 51000 Rijeka; tel. +385 51 336 445. The earlier address from a Zadar directory (…@ri.t-com.hr) is not used. The text is in Croatian with an English translation under it.*

⚠⚠ ***Sent by David on 4–5 November 2026 (the archive asked for his postal address, supplied 5 November); answered 6 November, above.***

rows.why:
**Answered 5 November 2026 by the friary itself (*doc*):** the parish of St George holds registers only from after the Second World War; everything earlier is at the State Archives in Rijeka. The Rijeka State Archives then reported on 6 November that the Trsat death register 1803–1815 has no entry for him (see errand 39). 

**Josephus (Josip) Defranceschi, parish priest of Draga 1798–1808, has no burial.** *Every Draga book on FamilySearch has been read for him (births, marriages, deaths, 4 November 2026) and none holds it.* **What is documented (`doc`):** he writes the Draga baptism book until 13 September 1808; on **29 September 1808** a Trsat Franciscan marries a couple *«de licentia M.R.D. Parochi Dragensis, qui actu infirmitate … Josephi Defranceschi»* with the foot note *«ob impotentiam Dni Parochi»*; and his successor Xanich calls him *«mei Praedecessoris Parochi defuncti»* in 1827. **So he died in the last days of September 1808 (`inf`).** The Draga dead were buried at **Trsat and Bakar** (no cemetery at Draga until 30 September 1855). Bakar, August–December 1808, is nil. **Trsat's death book is on FamilySearch for 1737–1803 and from November 1815, but not for 1803–1815: that gap is the question.**

**Why the convent and not only the state archive.** *The friars did the parish's work while the priest was ill: Fr Ruffinus Czohar marries at Draga on 29 September 1808 on his licence, and Fr Hyacinthus Rigetti signs the Draga baptism book as «V.P.» (vicar) from 21 September 1808.* **A friar who buried a priest of Draga would have written it in the convent's book, and a church book is not bound by the state's closing rules.** *It is an `inf` that the burial is at Trsat; the convent may simply say it holds nothing, which is also an answer.*

**Sister to [errand 39](/errands/#errand-39)**, the same question put to the Rijeka State Archives. Send both, or send this one first if the Franciscans are quicker.
rows.ask:
**In English, so the letter can be checked before it goes.** *It asks the guardian (or whoever keeps the books) whether the convent holds the Trsat death register for 1803–1815 or any record of burials in 1808, whether it contains an entry for the death of the Reverend Josephus Defranceschi, parish priest of Draga, in late September 1808, and for a transcript or a photograph of the entry with its date and the place of burial. It also asks whether the convent's chronicle (the* liber memorabilium *or similar) notes his death or the friars' service at Draga that autumn.*

⚠ ***Gmail draft saved 4 November 2026, not sent:*** *the convent publishes no e-mail address (the Visit Rijeka page lists only Frankopanski trg, 51000 Rijeka, tel. +385 51 452 900). The draft therefore goes to the Franciscan province's own office, **secprov@ofm.hr** (Kaptol 9, Zagreb, from ofm.hr), and asks the secretary to forward it to the guardian at Trsat. A tourist-guide e-mail for the convent exists but is not used. If the letter is posted instead, address it to the Guardian, Franjevački samostan, Frankopanski trg, 51000 Rijeka.*

⚠⚠ ***Forwarded through the Franciscan provincial's office on 4 November 2026; the friary's reply of 5 November is above.***

rows.draft:
Dear National Archives of Australia,

I am researching my family's history (a non-commercial, family-history study of the surname De Franceski / Defranceski) and would like to request access to, and a digital copy of, the following items:

1. Series D4881: the arrival/alien card for Anton Mario De Franceski (period 13 April 1949 to 31 December 1976, held in Adelaide). Please confirm the item before copying; the series is large.
2. Series B44, items V1978/151 and V1978/152: the naturalisation files of Zdravko De Franceski and Ruža De Franceski, Horsham, Victoria, 1978. I understand the access status is 'not yet examined'; please examine them for public access.

I am the family's researcher (David Defranceski) and will pay any copying fee. If any item is closed, I would be grateful to learn the reason and how to apply for access.

Thank you,
David Defranceski

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Rijeci — and the registry office (Matični ured) of Novi Vinodolski
rows.what: The marriage registers of Klenovica and of Ledenice for 1883–1890 (the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Ana Kalanj), and Crikvenica's marriage register of 1912
rows.ref: Državni arhiv u Rijeci (Vinodol parish books; Crikvenica's own volume is Povijesni arhiv Rijeka 275 (K4), inv. 110) · Matični ured Novi Vinodolski (what the archive has not taken in) · Klenovica / Ledenice marriages 1883–1890 · Crikvenica marriages 1912 · the fond is HR-DARI-275, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga», Državni arhiv u Rijeci, 1560–1947, which has a published analytical inventory (Senčić, «Inventar Zbirke matičnih knjiga Povijesnog arhiva Rijeka 1560.-1947.», Vjesnik Povijesnog arhiva Rijeka 38, 1996, pp. 315–387), not digitised · HDA-883's Ledenice run ENDS at births 1861, marriages 1865, deaths 1865 (Milić 2017), so the book is not at the state archives in Zagreb · by the 1998 ordinance Klenovica sat in the Novi Vinodolski registry district and Ledenice in its own until 2024, when the office was left with one district
rows.why:
**The likeliest home of the marriage, and it cannot be read from a screen.** *Anton Rudolf's baptism (born 20 January 1890, baptised 9 February) is in a Klenovica register catalogued «Matične knjige, Ledenice / Klenovica»; its remarks say the parents were at Klenovica only because they were staying with Ana's parents («kod roditelja žene Ane») at house 22, where the godfather Jakov Kalanj also lived (`doc`).* **Neither book is on FamilySearch:** Klenovica is not a parish in the FamilySearch tree, and Ledenice's marriage films stop at 1882. **Marriages are normally celebrated in the bride's parish (`inf`).** *The Geni tree puts Uršula Kovačina's marriage at Crikvenica on 21 June 1912 (`lore`, untested); Crikvenica's own marriage register for 1912 is the first place to look.* **The archive's pre-war registers are in Rijeka (the 1946/1949 custody rule; see the Trsat reply of 6 November 2026: their nil is their nil, not ours).** Worklist row 141.

**15 November 2026 — the nil at Zagreb is now documented and the fond is named.** *Milić's published inventory of HDA-883 lists Ledenice's seven volumes and they stop at 1865; the later FamilySearch films of Ledenice therefore came from another holder, and the likeliest is Rijeka's own collection, HR-DARI-275. Ask for it by that fond.*
rows.ask:
**In Croatian, to the State Archives in Rijeka, copied to the Matični ured of Novi Vinodolski.** *It asks whether the registers of Klenovica and of Ledenice for 1883–1890 and Crikvenica's marriages of 1912 are held, whether there is an entry for the marriage of Josip Defranceschi and Ana Kalanj (and for Petar Kovačina's daughter Uršula in 1912), and for a transcript or photograph with the date and the witnesses.*

⚠ ***Not sent; no address written.*** *Take the addresses from each office's own site. This is David's letter, not a film to read.*

2. upis o vjenčanju **Uršule Kovačina** (kći Petra i Marije rođ. Car, kuća 119, Crikvenica) i Antona Rudolfa Defranceschija, vjerojatno **Crikvenica, 1912.**

rows.ref: AT-OeStA/KA Marine NMA Pers OffBea Akten MGBBl 2651 (Defranceschi, Johann, geb. 1833, Geburtsort Gallignana) · AT-OeStA/AVA Justiz JM Präs. A 134.22 (Defranceschi, Carlo Dragutin, b. Zara 29.7.1883) · JM Präs. A 140.14 (Franceschi, Giovanni Pietro de, b. Rovigno 9.2.1854) · and whether JS DS 83.1.14 (Franceschi, Pietro, Almissa 1828–1843) and JS DS 80.3.4 (Franceschi, Antonio, Cattaro 1843) can be copied under their conservation restriction
rows.why: **A Marinegrundbuchblatt gives birthplace, parents, religion, marriage and children** — for a man born at Gračišće in 1833 that is a whole household, and this archive already holds his Pola marriage of 16 January 1871 and his children's naval-parish records. *The catalogue page for his file, and those of three neighbouring Marine person files, return a server error; the item layer under «Offiziere und Beamte» is undisplayable while sibling records load, so the signature must be confirmed by a person.* The two justice personal records are public, unrestricted and carry birthplace, parents and career; at €6 a scan they are the cheapest documents the archive can add. The first half-hour of handling is free, so the letter gives the signatures and asks nothing open-ended.
rows.ask: **In German, to the Kriegsarchiv and to the AVA/FHKA reading room, as two short letters.** *The first asks the Kriegsarchiv to confirm the current signature of the Marinegrundbuchblatt of Johann Defranceschi, born 1833 at Gallignana, whose catalogue page and those of three neighbouring Marine person files return a server error, and to quote for a scan; the «Personenanfrage Kriegsarchiv» form fits a man of 1820–1914 exactly. The second orders scans of two public, unrestricted personal records on the Reproauftrag form of 1 July 2025, which has «Land» fields for the delivery and the invoice address, and asks in the same breath whether the two conservation-blocked justice files can be copied.* E-mail. The Kriegsarchiv's «Personenanfrage Kriegsarchiv» form fits a man of 1820–1914 exactly; the AVA order goes on the Reproauftrag form of 1 July 2025, which has «Land» fields for both the delivery and the invoice address. Scans are delivered by download link after payment (€6 to A3, €12 to A1). The archive sends an offer with an estimate first, and the fee is payable even if the search finds nothing.

rows.who: Državni arhiv u Rijeci (the State Archives in Rijeka), copied to the City of Rijeka
rows.what: The decision that gave the port's quays their Croatian names, somewhere in 1945–55 — the one that should name both De Franceschijev gat and Visinov gat
rows.ref: Gradski narodni odbor Rijeka / Narodni odbor općine Rijeka, decisions on the naming of streets and port quays, about 1945–1955 · De Franceschijev gat (the former Gat Zichy, Hungarian era; Italian era in the same basin) · Visinov gat (the former Marija Valerija / Molo Napoli)
rows.why: **The pier carries this family's name and nobody has said which man it is.** *The Hungarian port named its quays for Maria Theresa, Adamić and the governors Zichy and Szápáry, then for the dynasty; the Italian administration used Italian city names. The De Franceschi name is therefore a* ***post-1945 Croatian naming***, *given in the same programme as Visinov gat — and a decree that names a sea captain beside him will almost certainly say what each man was. It is one document, and it would end a question three searches have failed to answer.* **⚠ Added 22 Nov 2026, before sending:** one chronology (Drinković 2015, its 1948 entry) says the pier was the *Gata Otokar Keršovani* in 1948 and is «danas» the De Franceschi pier, which would put the De Franceschi name later than 1945-55; one unsourced line, not yet confirmed. Consider widening the period in the letter («1945.–1995.») before it goes.
rows.ask: **In Croatian, to the archive's reference service.** *It asks for the naming decision (odluka/rješenje) of the city's people's committee for the port quays in 1945–55, or for the file in which such decisions were kept, and for a copy or a transcript of the paragraph naming De Franceschijev gat and Visinov gat.*

2. ako postoji, molim **presliku ili prijepis** onoga dijela u kojem se spominju **De Franceschijev gat** i **Visinov gat**;

rows.ref: Gologorica was in the diocese of Trieste–Capodistria for the whole span of the registers walked here (the bishop's own signature in the death book, [Gologorica line](/gologorica-line/)) · «visitatio canonica» of **7 July 1876**, named in the register by date · worklist 190
rows.why:
**The parish books are at Pazin; the bishop's papers about the parish are not, and this archive has never asked for them.** What that layer would hold: the **visitation protocols and decrees** (the 1876 visitation is dated in the register itself, the strongest handle an enquiry can have); **marriage dispensations** (consanguinity dispensations for a village this endogamous are a map of its cousin marriages); **ordination and priest files** (four priests of the surname this archive cannot place; three parish priests died in office at Gologorica); and **parish correspondence** (the 1835 collated copies, the 1836 collation certificate, the «Segue libro nuovo» of 1880).

**The first question is not about the name at all:** whether the pre-1977 papers of the Istrian parishes stayed at Trieste or went with the parishes to Poreč–Pula when the diocesan boundaries were redrawn. *This archive does not know which, and will not assume.* The letter therefore asks that first, and asks for the rest only if the answer is Trieste. If the answer is Poreč–Pula, [errand 48](/errands/#errand-48) already has an address there.

*Held since 6 October 2026 under David's standing hold; drafted now so it is ready, not so it goes.*

Gentile Direttore / Spettabile Archivio diocesano,

mi chiamo David Defranceski e ricostruisco, per ricerca familiare e senza scopo commerciale, la storia di una famiglia **De Franceschi / Defranceschi** della parrocchia di **Gologorica (Gologorizza), nel distretto di Pisino (Pazin), in Istria**.

Le matrici parrocchiali di Gologorica dal 1784 al 1880 (oggi presso l'Archivio di Stato di Pisino) mostrano che per tutto quel periodo la parrocchia dipendeva dalla **diocesi di Trieste e Capodistria**. Il registro dei morti ricorda inoltre una **visita canonica del 7 luglio 1876**.

Vorrei sapere, con la massima cortesia:

1. se l'Archivio diocesano conserva carte relative alla parrocchia di Gologorica per gli anni **1784–1880** (verbali e decreti di visita pastorale, in particolare quella del **7 luglio 1876**; dispense matrimoniali; corrispondenza con la parrocchia);
2. se conserva fascicoli di sacerdoti di cognome **De Franceschi / Defranceschi / de' Franceschi** della diocesi negli stessi anni;
3. se le carte delle parrocchie istriane anteriori al 1977 sono rimaste a Trieste oppure sono passate ad altro ente (ad esempio all'Archivio diocesano di Parenzo e Pola), e in tal caso a chi mi debba rivolgere;
4. quali siano le modalità e le eventuali spese per consultare o ottenere copia di tali documenti.

La ringrazio fin d'ora per l'attenzione.

Cordiali saluti,
David Defranceski
[indirizzo, Australia]

rows.what: The Gračišće marriage book 1836–1876 (Mattiasich × Defranceschi, about 1857) and the French-period civil registers of Pazin, 1812–1814
rows.ref: Gračišće MKV 1836–1876, listed by DAPA as digitised and held at the parish (Vlahov, Jelinčić, Doblanović, «Popis matičnih knjiga», *Vjesnik Istarskog arhiva* 11–13, 2008) · French takeover of the registers 20 July 1812 – 5 January 1814, entered by the priest on p. 38 of the Gologorica death book (ZM34K-214, M01069247) · worklist 298 and 180
rows.why:
**Two asks that [errand 38](/errands/#errand-38) does not carry.**

**(1) The Mattiasich marriage.** The Pazin baptisms of 1859, 1861 and 1863 (house 60) name a *Maria Leopoldina / Leopolda Defranceschi*, wife of the cursor *Joannes Mattiasich*. This archive reads her as the house-5 daughter of Joannes Baptista Defranceschi and Francisca Salomon, born at Gračišće on 17 November 1829 (`inf`). **A marriage entry naming her father and mother would turn that inference into a document.** The Gračišće marriage book for 1836–1876 is not in the family's copy of the Pazin films, the Record Atlas lists no FamilySearch volume for Gračišće, and FamilySearch's Pazin marriage book ends in 1852, so a marriage of about 1857 is on nothing this archive can open. Worklist 298.

**(2) The eighteen months the parish did not keep its books.** On p. 38 of the Gologorica death register the priest wrote that the registers were handed to the Municipality of Pazin on **20 July 1812** and returned on **5 January 1814**, and that he entered the interval's deaths afterwards («hic retuli»). **If the commune registered, there should be French civil registers of 1812–1813**, the only contemporary record of that window. The DAPA register list shows no civil series for Pazin; French-period communal fonds are listed for Buje, Labin, Novigrad, Poreč and Rovinj, none for Pazin, and the introduction says few survive. *Absence from a list is not proof*: the question is worth one line to the people who would know. Worklist 180.

It can go as a separate message, or be pasted into the one letter as items 5 and 6.

Poštovani,

nastavljam na svoj upit o mikrofilmovima ZM34K-214/215/217 i molim Vas pomoć oko još dvije stavke.

**1 · Matična knjiga vjenčanih župe GRAČIŠĆE, 1836.–1876.**
U Popisu matičnih knjiga (Vjesnik Istarskog arhiva 11–13, 2008.) ta je knjiga navedena kao digitalizirana, a čuva se u župnom uredu Gračišće. Tražim upis o vjenčanju **Ivana (Joannes) Mattiasicha, kurira (cursor), i Leopoldine Marije Defranceschi**, kćeri Ivana Krstitelja Defranceschija i Franciske rođ. Salomon iz kućnog broja 5 (rođene 17. studenoga 1829.), vjerojatno oko **1855.–1858.** Molim Vas presliku tog upisa, s obližnjim stranicama, ili obavijest kako je mogu dobiti. Zanima me i postoji li matična knjiga umrlih župe **Pazin 1847.–1882.** i je li dostupna.

**2 · Civilne matične knjige iz doba Ilirskih provincija**
U matičnoj knjizi umrlih župe Gologorica župnik je zabilježio da su knjige **20. srpnja 1812.** predane općini Pazin, a vraćene **5. siječnja 1814.** Postoje li u fondu **HR-DAPA-429** ili u drugim fondovima civilne matične knjige (rođeni, vjenčani, umrli) općine ili kantona Pazin za **1812.–1813.**, osobito za Gologoricu? Gdje su knjige preuzete 20. srpnja 1812. i vraćene 1814.? Je li primjerak otišao sudu prvog stupnja u Rovinju ili Trstu?

Riječ je o obiteljskom, **nekomercijalnom** istraživanju. Molim obavijest o cijeni, načinu plaćanja i potrebnom obrascu.

Unaprijed zahvaljujem.

S poštovanjem,
David Defranceski

rows.what: Anka Nera Defranceski (born Crikvenica 1915; married names Geiger, then Oreščanin), dead at Belgrade in 1944
rows.ref: Worklist 53 · searched and not found: Arolsen (16 September 2026), the Jasenovac named list (20 September), the Museum of Genocide Victims census at Belgrade (29 September; her married names not typed there, a gap in that nil, 13 November) · not yet asked: the 1944 death register of Belgrade, and the Banjica inmate books at the Historical Archives of Belgrade
rows.why:
**Born at Crikvenica in 1915, died at Belgrade in 1944, aged twenty-nine.** That is all the archive has. She married **Josip Geiger** (1911–1936) and then **Branko Oreščanin**, whose name she carries. **Her mother Ursula died at Belgrade too, in 1975**, so the city is the family's place, not a one-off. Three systems have said no (Arolsen, Jasenovac, the victims' census, the last typed only on the Defranc- spellings), so the **Belgrade death register for 1944** is the one document that can say where she was and how she died; and the **Banjica camp inmate books** are the one Belgrade institution that would record a detained woman. *A hypothesis, not a claim:* the Allied bombing of Belgrade on 16 April 1944 (`inf`), nothing ties her to it.

**A problem the letter has to meet:** as her great-nephew David is outside the list of those entitled to an extract from a registry of deaths and would need a decision under the law's appeal route (noted 13 November 2026). So the letter does not demand an extract; it asks **whether an entry exists, under what name, and what a descendant of the collateral line must submit to obtain a copy or a certificate.** *Have the Serbian text read by a Serbian speaker before it goes.*
rows.ask:
**In Serbian (Latin script), two short letters on one page, one to each office.** *(A) To the registrar's service of the city: does the death register of Belgrade for 1944 hold an entry for Anka Oreščanin née Defranceski, born at Crikvenica in 1915, and under what name and date; what documents does a descendant of her brother need to obtain a copy or a certificate; is a transcript or confirmation of the entry's existence possible without the full extract. (B) To the Historical Archives of Belgrade: do the Banjica camp inmate books or any 1944 civil record name her; how to request a search.* ⚠⚠ ***NOT SENT. rows.who: Archivio di Stato di Trieste — fondo «Governatorato della Venezia Giulia poi Commissariato generale civile per la Venezia Giulia»
rows.what: The act of 10 December 1920, protocol N. 1x-4411/563, that cites the 1626 birth certificate of Leonardo De Franceschi of Luincis
rows.ref: Gologorica baptism register, folio 142, typed slip (DAPA ZM34K-214, M01069151; entry beneath it M01069152: Victor Richardus Defranceschi, born 15 June 1871, «vide … sub 30 protocoll.») · Archivio di Stato di Trieste, *Guida aggiornata al 31 dicembre 2025*, p. 28: Commissariato generale civile, bb. 547 e regg. 350 (1918–1922), series *Gabinetto*, *Archivio generale* (bb. 412), *Protocolli, indici e rubriche* (regg. 340, inventario parziale) · M. E. Hametz, «The Nefarious Former Authorities: Name Change in Trieste, 1918–22», *Austrian History Yearbook* 35 (2004), cites «CGCVG, Atti Generali, 1919–22, busta 82» (footnote not read here) · worklist 179
rows.why:
**The biggest single lead on David's own line, and the cheapest to ask.** A typed slip pasted across the Gologorica baptism of Victor Richardus Defranceschi quotes a **letter of the Commissariato Generale Civile per la Venezia Giulia, 10 December 1920, N. 1x-4411/563** (signed on the Commissariato's order by Avv. Melone), which says the original spelling of the surname is «de Franceschi» **«ciò che risulta dalla fede di nascita del suo proavo Leonardo De Franceschi nato a Luincio dd. 23/6 1626»**. The file behind that letter should contain, or cite, the **birth certificate itself**: the only document that names a man of this family in 1626.

**Four handles, so one search is enough:** the fondo and series in the archive's own words; the protocol number and date; the person it concerns (Victor Richardus, born 15 June 1871, then forty-nine); and Hametz's busta 82 as a cross-reference. The fondo is open (the «esclusi dalla consultazione» list is a nine-day maintenance closure, 26 February – 6 March 2026, *not* a restriction).

**Discipline.** It is a 1920 ruling, not a 1626 record; «proavo» is loose; an office regularising surnames after annexation wanted a spelling settled, which is not a proved descent. *No generation has been added to the Carnia chain on the strength of it, and none will be until the file or the book is read.*

Gentile Direttore / Spettabile Archivio di Stato di Trieste,

mi chiamo David Defranceski e studio, per ricerca familiare e senza scopo commerciale, una famiglia **De Franceschi** della parrocchia di **Gologorica (Pisino, Istria)**.

Il registro dei battesimi della parrocchia reca, incollato al foglio 142, un foglietto dattiloscritto che cita una lettera del **Commissariato Generale Civile per la Venezia Giulia del 10 dicembre 1920, N. 1x-4411/563** («D'Ordine del Commissariato Gen. Civ. — Avv. Melone»). La lettera dichiara che la grafia originale del cognome del battezzato è «**de Franceschi**», «ciò che risulta dalla fede di nascita del suo proavo **Leonardo De Franceschi nato a Luincio dd. 23/6 1626**». Il battezzato è **Victor Richardus Defranceschi, nato il 15 giugno 1871**; a margine del registro si legge «vide … sub 30 protocoll.».

Le sarei molto grato se potesse dirmi:

1. se, tramite i registri di protocollo e gli indici del fondo *Governatorato della Venezia Giulia poi Commissariato generale civile* (serie «Protocolli, indici e rubriche»), il numero di protocollo e la data indicati conducano a un fascicolo nell'«Archivio generale» o nel «Gabinetto»;
2. se il fascicolo relativo alla **restituzione del cognome «de Franceschi»** per Victor Richardus Defranceschi (Gologorica, 1871) si sia conservato e se contenga la **fede di nascita di Leonardo De Franceschi (Luincio, 23 giugno 1626)** o una copia o trascrizione;
3. se sia a questo scopo la serie «Atti Generali» (busta 82, come citata in letteratura) o altra;
4. come e a quale costo sia possibile ottenerne una riproduzione.

La ringrazio per l'attenzione e resto a disposizione per ogni ulteriore dato.

Cordiali saluti,
David Defranceski
[indirizzo, Australia]

rows.what: The baptism of Ana Grubišić (Ana Nana), given as born 1876 at Omiš, daughter of Nicolaus (Niko) Grubišić, later the wife of Josip (Bepo) Franceschi of Perinuša: which Omiš-district baptism registers of 1870–1882 the archive holds, and a search for her entry
rows.ref: Omiš (Almissa) births 1850–1880, FamilySearch waypoint 9R2C-3Y9, images 183–234 (1873–1879) read on the page on 22 November 2026: no Ana, no Nicolaus Grubišić (`doc`, a nil for that parish and those years) · Podgrađe (Omiš) 1825–1832, Tugare births to 1865, Duće marriages only, Zakučac births to 1850: no 1870s birth book on FamilySearch · the FamilySearch name index has no Ana Grubišić at Omiš · the family's captions (Jagul Wine Cellar, Stari Imotski) and David's word (18 November 2026) give her as 1876–1945; the tree's father «Nicholaus (Niko) Grubišić» and her birth at Omiš are the tree's word (`lore`) · worklist 341
rows.why: **It is the one record that would turn Ana Nana from a caption into a person.** Her dates (1876–1945) rest on two family captions and a family confirmation; no register names her. The Omiš town parish book is read for 1873–1879 and she is not in it, so either she was baptised in another parish of the Omiš district (the villages above Omiš, Zakučac, Gata, Podgrađe, Duće and others had their own books) or her year is not what the captions say. FamilySearch has none of those books for the 1870s; the State Archives' copies are the next place. An entry would give her baptism date, her parents' names and place of residence, and the godparents (often a relative). *No kinship to this archive's lines is claimed; this is a separate family.*
